A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Word4Per, ZS-CPR and the ITCPR benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite changes in title, authorship and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports original ITCPR retrieval experiments, ablations, CUHK-PEDES fine-tuning results and supplementary fusion/efficiency measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original retrieval and supplementary experiments and adds evaluated baselines and prompt/token-length results.

M1.justification: The two-stage CLIP/TINet framework, losses, final single-token query and fusion procedure remain unchanged. The optimal-depth networks and fusion emphasized in v2 were already described and tested in v1 Appendices A and C.

E1.justification: LTCC is newly used to train the Simple-CCReID comparator in v2 Section 5.2. ITCPR evaluation coverage and Word4Per's image-caption/IPR training pools remain; the other-dataset descriptions move to Appendix B.2.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds SEARLE-XL under original and fine-tuned CLIP, and Text+Model C using Simple-CCReID under both backbones. This materially broadens comparisons to another ZS-CIR approach and an explicit clothes-changing alternative. Pic2Word and the original unimodal/averaging baselines remain.

E3.justification: The main comparison switches from v1's standard three-layer TINets to the previously supplementary optimal configurations: two layers for visual supervision and three for textual supervision. V2 also tests different query templates and token lengths of 1, 2, 4 and 8. The benchmark, metrics and stated training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds template/token-length ablations in Table 2, but removes v1 Table 4's systematic dataset-mixture/resolution-filtering sweep and the direct joint-training-versus-fusion comparison in Table B and Figure F. Architecture, qualitative, data-fraction and fusion-efficiency studies largely remain, often relocated; some mixed/filtered-data results survive in the efficiency study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The practice of reporting single performance values is unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds comparator and template/token results, revises visual-loss ablation values, and removes dataset-quality and joint-training entries. For example, visual-loss ITC Rank-1 changes from 34.968 to 35.786 alongside revised architecture settings. Optimized visual-loss/fusion scores promoted into v2 Table 1 already appear in v1 Table B; the best supplementary Rank-1 of 47.502 is unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical loss definitions and identity-matching assumptions are retained. V1 Equations 6–7 are merely grouped into v2 Equation 6; no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the CPR/ZS-CPR task, two-stage Word4Per without CPR-triplet training, ITCPR benchmark and claimed advantage exceeding 10%. The added experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds a linguistic-instability explanation for long-token degradation and revises the visual-loss data-scaling interpretation. It removes the detailed quality-versus-quantity and joint-training explanations. The semantic-versus-background interpretation and limitation concerning consistent facial/body features remain.

D1.justification: Reported training times change from approximately 5/11 hours to 2/5 hours for ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14. V2 adds LTCC training information for the clothes-changing baseline and removes v1's feature-caching suggestion. The repository link and future code/data-release promise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gu et al.'s clothes-changing person re-identification work for the new comparator. The SEARLE and LTCC source works were already cited in v1; the additional LTCC bibliography entry duplicates an existing work. The broader related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: architecture and qualitative studies move into Sections 5.3–5.4, while loss/data-fraction studies and other-dataset descriptions move into the appendix. The title, author list and Outlook heading also change, alongside prose editing.

P2.justification: V2 adopts ACM formatting with revised author blocks, headers and caption/table typography. Table 1 expands and the data-fraction table is reorganized side by side. Existing figures move and merge, including v1 Figure B and Figure 4 into v2 Figure 6; joint-loss panels and two semantic examples disappear.

improvement.justification: The new SEARLE-XL and clothes-changing comparisons strengthen validation of the central retrieval claim, while Table 2 supplies evidence for prompt/token choices. This is a limited net gain: the strongest retrieval scores already existed in v1, useful data-quality and joint-training analyses are removed, and v2 Table 1 labels fusion less clearly than v1 Table B.
